newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Cocoa's uptrend seen intact.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Cocoa's uptrend seen intact.

text.p: JULY Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
LIFFE cocoa managed to hold onto its uptrend after Wednesday's late comeback to close near session highs.
July ended up 12 stg at 1,038 stg per tonne on Wednesday, bolstered by trade buying. It was called to open three down on Thursday morning.
Adrian Haylor, analyst at Sucden, said cocoa could slip a bit further but that he was generally friendly toward the market because it held several support levels this week.
July has held an up trendline reaching back to late February that intersected with the recent April 9 low of 980. He said he was impressed with July's bounced off support at 1,006, Tuesday's low.
On Wednesday, July also managed to hold suport at 1,003, the 40-day moving average. Wednesday's low was just above that at 1,004.

Some shorter-term indicators also showed encouraging signs. He pointed out that July broke up and out of the 20-day moving average at 1,030 to reach a session high close of 1,038 and shook off a downward pointing relative strength index (RSI).

Although bears can make a case for lower cocoa prices by arguing that the recent move up has lacked volume and that July still had to break resistance at 1,045 by the end of the week to keep momentum to the upside intact, Haylor said "there's some room to be optimistic because the longer-term trends have held."

A U.S. analyst was also optimistic on cocoa but said the near-term was tricky because CSCE cocoa still looked like it was bottoming out on daily charts. He said "we still like the long-term potential upside for (CSCE July cocoa at) 1,580, but we are not sure whether the downside is done yet."
